elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence permits either Party to assign only "to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice"; there is no no-consent affiliate carve-out for IBM. The only affiliate mechanic retained is MSL-side ("MSL may assign or subcontract ... to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent"). Defect: no operative permission for IBM to assign to an IBM affiliate without MSL approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the other Party" — notice only, no consent, and the following sentence is subordinated by "Otherwise".

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "Otherwise, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party" binds MSL to obtain IBM's approval for all non-successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent sentence now ends "...without prior written approval by the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld"; the retained MSL Related Company sentence uses the same standard ("not be unreasonably withheld or delayed").

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor restriction appears anywhere in the rendered language; MSL may assign to a successor (including an IBM competitor) on bare written notice. Defect: add an express bar on MSL assignment to an IBM competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply on the cited text: neither §16.2 as rendered nor §16.5 (which is MSL-side only — MSL must notify IBM and procure successor assumption) confers any MSL termination or re-pricing right on an IBM change of control, so there is nothing to delete.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets..." — expressly mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "...upon written notice to the other Party."

"Otherwise, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties ... without prior written approval by the other Party." The one retained non-successor exception (MSL Related Company) is itself consent-conditioned ("with IBM's prior written consent"), so it is not a no-consent exception that would defeat this element; the previously duplicative MSL-only bar was folded into the mutual sentence.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...which shall not be unreasonably withheld" appended to the mutual consent sentence, consistent with the retained "not be unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard for MSL Related Company assignments.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all four elements (mutual successor assignment, written notice, consent for other assignments, reasonableness standard) appear in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred is not complete — two elements missing: (i) no no-consent affiliate carve-out for IBM, and (ii) no prohibition on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor. These would need express operative wording if the preferred level were targeted.

Minimality holds: one inserted successor sentence plus a five-word reasonableness qualifier. Deletion of the redundant MSL-only sentence ("MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM") is necessary rather than cosmetic — retained unqualified, it would contradict both the new mutual successor right and the new not-unreasonably-withheld standard. No survival tails, procedures, or out-of-checklist requirements were added.

Intent preserved: MSL's Related Company consent mechanic survives intact; §16.5 (MSL sale/merger notification and successor assumption warranty) is untouched and remains consistent with the new successor mechanic; the MSL-only bars in the Loan Agreement and confidentiality terms are left in place. No dangling cross-references or undefined terms are introduced (the trailing "MSL shall" is a pre-existing excerpt truncation, not an artifact of the edit).

Note for the drafter: the mutual successor right is a genuine concession — MSL may now assign to its own successor on bare notice, without the competitor screen the preferred position would supply. If MSL will accept it, adding "provided that no assignment may be made to a competitor of the other Party" would recover part of the preferred position at low cost.
